#1. Vectors
# the price of tomato, potato and meat in 2017 August were 300 400 and 3000 AMD per kilo, respectively. In the same period of 2018 hey became 200, 350,3700.

# 1.1. construct vectors assigning names of the food types.
price2017<-c(300, 400,3000)
price2018<-c(200, 350, 3700)
names(price2017)<-c("tomato", "potato", "meat")

# 1.2. calculate percentage change of the prices for each product.

perc_change<-(price2018-price2017)/price2017



# 1.3  Construct a logical vector to illustrate for what products the negative change was more than by 10%
perc_change>=-0.1

# 1.4. Calculate the average change in prices of these 3 products
mean(perc_change)
# the mean percentage change was -7.5%

# 2. Matrix

# 2.1. Construct a matrix which stores the heights of 1st, 5th, 10th class girls' and boys' averafe heights respectively.
class1<-c(112, 108)
class5<-c(135, 134)
class10<-c(158, 165)
all<-c(class1, class5, class10)
heights<-matrix(all, nrow=3, byrow=TRUE)

# 2.2. assign names to the rows and columns
gender<-c("girls", "boys")
class<-c("1class", "5class", "10class")
colnames(heights)<-gender
rownames(heights)<-class

# 2.3. calculate the average height of pupils at each class
means<-rowMeans(heights)

# 2.4. subset the heights of girls only
girls<-heights[,1]

# 3. Data Frames

# 3.1. load the dataset Iris from R built-in datasets
data(iris)

# 3.2. examine the structure of the dataframe
str(iris)

# 3.3. how many of the  species have a petal length not more than 3.5
nrow(iris[iris$Petal.Length<=3.5,])
# There are 55 such species

# 3.4. create a subset  of this dataframe which contains only setosas and for which the sepal length is less than 5.8 
subset<-iris[iris$species=="setosa" & iris$Sepal.Length<5.8,]

# 4. EXamining Dilijan Hotels dataset

# 4.1. read the file Dilijan hotels.csv in R which contains iformatin about accommodations listings which are in Dilijan from Tripadivosr
Dilijan<-read.csv("Dilijan hotels.csv, header=TRUE")

# 4.2. How many Bed and Breakfast type accommodations are found in the database?
table(Dilijan$Type)
# 38 Bed and Breakfast

# 4.3. What type of accommodations have overview rates of 5?
overview_5<-Dilijan[Dilijan$overview==5,]
table(overview_5$type)
# 5 Bed and Breakfast, 3 Lodge, 2 Specialty Lodging

# 4.4. replace NAs of the price variable with the 
Dilijan$Price[which(is.na(Dilijan$Price))]<-mean(Dilijan$Price, na.rm = TRUE)

# 4.4. Calculate the average prices of the hotels with an overview of less than 3.7
low<-subset(Dilijan, overview<3.7, )
mean(low$Price)
#The average price is aroung 47 USD
